newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom down on overseas venture worries.
newsitem.headline: Telekom down on overseas venture worries.

text.p: The shares of Telekom Malaysia Bhd remained weak in late-afternoon trading on concerns over its overseas ventures and on profit taking, dealers and analysts said.
Around 0800 GMT, the stock was down 40 cents to 12.10 ringgit on volume of nearly 1.5 million.
"They are very aggressive overseas, but they have to fork out a lot of money," said a dealer at Hwang-DBS Securities.
The stock was also sold down to reflect the weakness of other blue chip stocks following recent gains, dealers said.
Telekom earlier this week announced it was buying a 20.12 percent stake in Thailand's Samart Corp Plc.
Analysts said Samart was not as profitable as they had originally hoped.

Newspaper reports on Wednesday quoted Telekom's chief executive officer Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali in Bangkok as saying the company is bidding in telecommunications privatisation deals in Kenya and Zimbabwe and was looking at other deals in foreign countries.

"Perhaps one should take profit now because the magnitude of foreign investments of two billion ringgit is quite chunky. Yes, we are talking about long term profit but it will drain cashflow," said a telecommunications analyst.
Telekom recently bought a 12 percent stake in Telkom South Africa for 504.4 million ringgit.
